documents.title: Orion architecture review — April
documents.content: Load testing showed p95 latency above the 500ms target at enterprise concurrency. Noisy-neighbor effects appeared in the shared inference gateway. The review recommended isolated inference cells for high-value customers.

documents.title: Orion security review — May
documents.content: Security review made customer-controlled inference and stronger tenant isolation release requirements for regulated workloads. External model calls require an explicit policy decision and auditable routing.

documents.title: Orion rollout plan — September
documents.content: Private inference cells are now the default for regulated workloads. Remaining delivery work: GPU scheduling, automated failover, and a clearer operator experience for deployment health.

documents.title: Atlas operating model
documents.content: Atlas focuses on deterministic enterprise workflow automation with human approval for irreversible actions and audit trails for every workflow run.

documents.title: Northstar discovery notes
documents.content: Customers describe the same problem: knowledge is fragmented across chat, docs, ticketing, code, meetings and CRM. They want AI to understand institutional context, not just retrieve snippets.

documents.title: Orion customer requirements matrix
documents.content: Acme requires customer-controlled inference. Helix requires internal-only access, auditability and separation between employee groups. Lumen is comfortable with managed AI for non-sensitive workflows.

documents.title: Decision memory design
documents.content: Memories should preserve who, what, when, why, confidence and evidence. The same fact can change over time; current truth must be distinguishable from historical truth.

documents.title: Permissions model draft
documents.content: Access is evaluated before retrieval and again before answer composition. Agents inherit explicit scopes rather than defaulting to the employee's full clearance.

documents.title: Atlas incident retrospective
documents.content: A stale CRM field caused an automation to select the wrong workflow branch. The fix added source freshness metadata and a human approval step for ambiguous account state.

documents.title: Executive thesis — Private Company Brain
documents.content: The product should become a private organizational intelligence layer: living memory, graph context, temporal decisions, permission-aware retrieval and model routing under customer control. Do not position as another chatbot.

messages.text: The shared gateway is fine for demos, but at enterprise concurrency the noisy-neighbor behavior is real. We should isolate the inference path.
For regulated workloads, I am not comfortable with silent external model routing. Policy needs to be explicit and auditable.
Acme's expansion depends on customer-controlled inference. They keep repeating that their prompts and operational data cannot cross the trust boundary.
The company brain cannot just return documents. It has to explain relationships, decisions, time and evidence.
We should evaluate permissions before retrieval so confidential memories never enter the model context by accident.
The Atlas incident is why freshness needs to travel with memory. A fact without time context can be actively dangerous.

memories.text: Orion's current default for regulated workloads is customer-controlled private inference. Remaining work is mostly scheduler, failover and operator reliability.
The move from shared inference to isolated cells was driven by measurable noisy-neighbor latency and later strengthened by security requirements for customer-controlled data isolation.
Northstar should behave like a private organizational intelligence layer, not another enterprise chatbot. Core concepts are memory, graph, time, evidence and permissions.
Acme expansion is blocked primarily by trust-boundary concerns: customer-controlled inference and private handling of sensitive prompts.
Agent/workflow context must carry freshness. Stale facts can route an otherwise correct automation down the wrong path.

decisions.title: Adopt isolated private inference cells
decisions.rationale: Reduce noisy-neighbor risk and prepare for customer-controlled deployment.

decisions.title: Require explicit model-routing policy for regulated workloads
decisions.rationale: Regulated data must not silently cross the company's trust boundary.

decisions.title: Make private deployment the default for regulated customers
decisions.rationale: Customer evidence and security requirements converged on private deployment as the safer default.

decisions.title: Build around organizational memory, not generic chat
decisions.rationale: Customers need relationships, temporal truth, evidence and permissions across systems.
